Steps.Title: Assign a compliance policy for each platform in use
Steps.Summary: Intune can mark a device compliant only when a compliance policy covers its platform.
Steps.Unchecked: No Maester check yet. The Zero Trust Assessment pack checks it (ZTA.24541 to ZTA.24547) once its results can name steps.

Sources.Note: Compliance policies set the rules each platform's devices must meet, and Conditional Access acts on the compliance state they produce.
Device-based Conditional Access starts with compliance policies, one per platform, because the policy can only act on the status they report.

Steps.Title: Turn on automatic Intune enrollment for Windows
Steps.Summary: Windows devices enroll in Intune when users join or register them in Microsoft Entra ID.
Steps.Unchecked: No Maester check yet. The Zero Trust Assessment pack checks it (ZTA.24546) once its results can name steps.

Sources.Note: Automatic enrollment enrolls Windows devices in Intune as they join or register with Microsoft Entra ID.

Steps.Title: Devices that sign in are compliant
Steps.Summary: Most devices that sign in are enrolled in Intune and marked compliant, so requiring compliance blocks few users.
Steps.Unchecked: No Maester check yet. A readiness check that reports the share of compliant devices is planned.

Sources.Note: Only devices registered in Microsoft Entra ID and enrolled in Intune can be marked compliant, so unenrolled devices fail a compliant-device policy.

Steps.Title: Mark devices with no compliance policy as not compliant
Steps.Summary: A device that no compliance policy covers can't pass Conditional Access by default.

Sources.Note: When Conditional Access uses compliance, review the tenant setting that decides how devices with no compliance policy are marked.

Steps.Title: Configure Windows Hello for Business on Windows devices
Steps.Summary: Users set up a Windows Hello for Business key on their PCs and sign in with a PIN or biometric.
Steps.Unchecked: No Maester check yet. The Zero Trust Assessment pack checks it (ZTA.24551) once its results can name steps.

Sources.Note: Give users a portable passkey first. They can then use it to set up Windows Hello for Business on each PC.
Intune gets Windows devices ready for Windows Hello for Business by delivering its policy settings at enrollment and keeping them in place after.

Steps.Title: Configure Platform SSO with the Secure Enclave key on macOS
Steps.Summary: Mac users sign in with a hardware-bound key that counts as a phishing-resistant method.
Steps.Unchecked: No Maester check yet. The Zero Trust Assessment pack checks it (ZTA.24568) once its results can name steps.

Sources.Note: Platform SSO is set with an Intune settings catalog policy, best assigned as users enroll their Macs. Secure Enclave is the recommended method.

Steps.Title: Connect Defender for Endpoint to Intune
Steps.Summary: Defender for Endpoint and Intune share device data, so Intune can receive the risk level Defender gives each device.
Steps.Unchecked: No check yet. MT.1098 reports connector health, but it skips or passes when the Defender for Endpoint connector is missing.

Sources.Note: Turn on the Intune connection in the Defender portal's advanced features, then check that Intune shows the connection as enabled. It can take about 15 minutes.
The integration has to be on in both Defender for Endpoint and Intune before Intune can use Defender's device data.

Steps.Title: Turn on compliance policy evaluation in the Defender for Endpoint connector
Steps.Summary: Compliance policies for Windows, iOS/iPadOS and Android can use the risk level that Defender for Endpoint reports for those devices.
Steps.Unchecked: No Maester check yet. The Zero Trust Assessment pack checks the Android toggle only (ZTA.24871).

Sources.Note: Once the connection shows enabled, turn on compliance policy evaluation for each platform in the connector. Each platform has its own toggle.
Defender's own walkthrough checks the connection and the platform's compliance toggle before it builds the compliance policy.

Steps.Title: Require a Defender for Endpoint machine risk score in compliance policies
Steps.Summary: Devices that Defender for Endpoint rates above the allowed risk level are marked noncompliant.
Rollout: Set the threshold to Low, the level most organizations use. High blocks nothing and only reports.
Assign the policy to a test group and confirm that its devices report the expected compliance state.
Widen the assignment. Where a compliant-device policy is on, risky devices lose access as soon as they are marked noncompliant.

Sources.Note: A platform's compliance policies use the connector's data only while that platform's toggle is on.
Connect the services, onboard devices, then add the risk rule to compliance. Conditional Access then blocks the devices marked noncompliant.
The risk score is one setting in each platform's compliance policy, so set up those policies first. Low suits most organizations; High only reports.
